1. Final Project Overview

Modern software developers lack dedicated social platforms tailored for technical discussions, code snippet sharing, and interactive portfolio discovery. Mainstream platforms prioritize algorithmic clickbait, while personal portfolio sites lack discovery mechanisms.

VOID is a specialized, developer-first social network combining developer portfolios, technical discussions, and an interactive terminal environment. The application is built with Next.js 16 (React 19) and stores all data natively in MongoDB using the official Node.js driver.

Key Features

  • Dual GUI & CLI Authentication: Standard credentials login plus an in-browser interactive terminal running void shell v1.0.0 with session.start capability.
  • Technical Feed: Reverse-chronological feed with code snippet rendering, copy-to-clipboard, post type badges, and category filters.
  • Project Discovery: Showcase open-source repositories and live web applications filtered by multikey technology stacks (TypeScript, Rust, Go, Python, WebGL, etc.).
  • Explore Leaderboards: Real-time trending technologies aggregation and engagement-weighted popular discussions.
  • Social Graph & Bookmarks: Follower/following relationships, atomic likes, threaded comments, and private bookmark libraries.

2. Final NoSQL Database & Data Model

The persistence layer is structured across 8 dedicated collections in MongoDB (void_db). The schema leverages document-oriented embedding for bounded sub-entities, while referencing high-velocity collections to guarantee sub-10ms queries without unbounded document growth.

2.1 Entity Relationship & Collections Summary

Collection Primary Key Key Indexed Fields Purpose
users _id (ObjectId) username (Unique), email (Unique), createdAt Developer accounts, bcrypt password hashes, skills, and denormalized counters
posts _id (ObjectId) createdAt (-1), authorId, tags (Multikey), popularity Technical discussions, embedded code snippets, and tags
projects _id (ObjectId) technologies (Multikey), authorId, createdAt Showcase repositories, technology stack arrays, and live demo links
comments _id (ObjectId) postId, createdAt (1), authorId Threaded discussion replies associated with posts
likes _id (ObjectId) userId + targetType + targetId (Compound Unique) Edge collection guaranteeing zero duplicate likes
follows _id (ObjectId) followerId + followingId (Compound Unique) Directed social graph edges between developers
bookmarks _id (ObjectId) userId + itemType + itemId (Compound Unique) Private saved library for posts and projects
notifications _id (ObjectId) recipientId + read + createdAt Activity alert stream for interactions and follows

2.2 Embedding vs. Referencing Design Decisions

Entity Pattern Justification & Trade-off Analysis
Code Snippets Embedded in posts Bounded size (<10KB), immutable relative to the post body, and always fetched simultaneously. Eliminates relational join overhead during feed rendering.
Tags & Skills Embedded arrays Small, bounded arrays (2 to 8 items). Multikey B-Tree indexes allow instant filtering without junction tables (e.g. post_tags).
Comments Referenced collection High-traffic discussions can receive thousands of replies. Embedding comments as an unbounded array would risk exceeding MongoDB's 16MB limit and cause memory reallocations.
Likes & Follows Referenced edge collections Enforces idempotency and prevents race conditions through atomic $inc and compound unique indexes.

3. Important MongoDB Queries

VOID contains 7 individually executable demonstration scripts located in scripts/queries/. Every query executes against live MongoDB data.

Query 1: Paginated Feed with Author Join (npm run query:posts)

Fetches reverse-chronological feed with author profile details joined in a single round-trip using $lookup and $unwind.

db.collection("posts").aggregate([
  { $sort: { createdAt: -1 } },
  { $skip: (page - 1) * limit },
  { $limit: limit },
  {
    $lookup: {
      from: "users",
      localField: "authorId",
      foreignField: "_id",
      as: "authorDetails"
    }
  },
  { $unwind: "$authorDetails" },
  {
    $project: {
      title: 1, type: 1, tags: 1, likesCount: 1, commentsCount: 1, createdAt: 1,
      author: { name: "$authorDetails.name", username: "$authorDetails.username", avatar: "$authorDetails.avatar" }
    }
  }
])

Query 2: Multikey Stack Filtering on Projects (npm run query:projects)

Uses multikey B-Tree index on technologies array to filter projects with sub-millisecond execution.

db.collection("projects").aggregate([
  { $match: { technologies: { $in: ["TypeScript"] } } },
  { $sort: { starsCount: -1 } },
  {
    $lookup: { from: "users", localField: "authorId", foreignField: "_id", as: "author" }
  },
  { $unwind: "$author" }
])

Query 4: Engagement Score Aggregation over Time Range (npm run query:popular)

Ranks discussions created in the last 30 days based on computed popularity: Score = (likesCount * 2) + (commentsCount * 3).

db.collection("posts").aggregate([
  { $match: { createdAt: { $gte: thirtyDaysAgo } } },
  {
    $addFields: {
      popularityScore: {
        $add: [
          { $multiply: [{ $ifNull: ["$likesCount", 0] }, 2] },
          { $multiply: [{ $ifNull: ["$commentsCount", 0] }, 3] }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  { $sort: { popularityScore: -1 } },
  { $limit: 5 }
])

Query 5: Trending Technologies Across Repositories (npm run query:tech)

Deconstructs array elements into stream documents, grouping by technology to calculate frequency and cumulative stars.

db.collection("projects").aggregate([
  { $unwind: "$technologies" },
  {
    $group: {
      _id: "$technologies",
      projectCount: { $sum: 1 },
      totalStars: { $sum: "$starsCount" },
      sampleProjects: { $push: "$title" }
    }
  },
  { $sort: { projectCount: -1, totalStars: -1 } },
  { $limit: 10 }
])

Query 7: Execution Plan Analysis (npm run query:explain)

Verifies index utilization using .explain("executionStats").

Winning Plan Stage : FETCH
Input Stage        : IXSCAN
Index Used         : idx_projects_technologies

6. Limitations & Future Scope

Limitations: Full-text search currently relies on indexed regex and B-Tree text weights. Integrating MongoDB Atlas Search Lucene analyzers would enable fuzzy autocomplete and spell tolerance. Real-time notifications operate through polling.

Future Scope: WebAssembly code execution sandboxes inside posts, direct GitHub webhook synchronization for commit statistics, and Atlas Vector Search for semantic developer recommendations.

Key Viva Questions & Answers

Q: Why choose MongoDB over PostgreSQL for this application?
A: Developer posts possess heterogeneous, semi-structured content (code snippets with arbitrary language syntax and variable arrays of technology tags). MongoDB enables embedding bounded snippets directly while multikey B-Tree indexes index array elements without requiring complex junction tables.
Q: How do you prevent duplicate likes or follows under concurrent requests?
A: By defining unique compound indexes on { userId: 1, targetType: 1, targetId: 1 } for likes and { followerId: 1, followingId: 1 } for follows. MongoDB atomically enforces uniqueness and rejects duplicates with error code 11000.
Q: How do you prove that your indexes are effective?
A: By running npm run query:explain. The winning execution plan reports stage IXSCAN on idx_projects_technologies with totalDocsExamined: 5 and nReturned: 5 (Ratio: 1.0), confirming zero full collection scans.
